blocks.text: The built-in acts: ctx.emit(<name>, payload, { audience? }): rendered on every client that hears it; your own event names reach on(). Positions are world meters, durations seconds (a haptic rumble's times are ms, as the Gamepad API's), colors a Color; an act that answers a handle answers it from…

ActPayloads = { damageNumber: { // a number `value` or any string `text` ("MISS", "+4 tomatoes"): one is enough; red below 0; `lifetime` the seconds it stays position: Vec3 value?: number text?: string color?: Color crit?: boolean size?: number = 1 lifetime?: number = 1.5 } playSound: { // answers the sound's handle: emit("stopSound", { soundId }) ends it, loops included; with `position` it is heard from that spot at `volume` out to refDistance (default a sixth of maxDistance, at least 4 m and at most half of it), falling to silence at maxDistance (the audible reach in meters); without one it is the acting player's own; mode "restart" replaces this object's still-playing copy of that clip instead of stacking clip: string position?: Vec3 volume?: number = 1 pitch?: number = 1 loop?: boolean mode?: "overlap" | "restart" bus?: string priority?: number maxDistance?: number refDistance?: number follow?: boolean onPlaying?: string | ((ctx: ObjectAPI, sound: { soundId: string; clip: string; durationSeconds?: number }) => unknown) // an export of this script, run once as (ctx, sound) when the sound's first sample plays; durationSeconds is absent while the clip's length is unknown } stopSound: { soundId: string } preload: { refs: string[] } // warms each sound, texture or model before its first use on the machines that hear it (the acting player's by default), so a game loads ahead of a moment it sees coming: emit it when those assets become likely; only machines in the room when it is sent hear it, so a room with no player in it warms no player, and one that joins later is not warmed; fire-and-forget, nothing shown, the world unchanged fx: { // an effect script you wrote (scripts/effects/*.fx.js) spawned as an OBJECT at a point, answers its id (tagged "fx"): patch it through getObject(id).fx.params.heat = 0.2 (the effect re-runs), end a loop with destroy(id) (a finished one-shot removes itself); params / seed feed the effect export; attachTo: <id> parents it to that object: it appears at `position`, rides the target's transform and dies with it (the impact pattern: a burn on whatever the projectile hit) position: Vec3 script: string params?: Record<string, unknown> seed?: number tags?: string[] attachTo?: string } decal: { // a lasting mark projected onto the surface at the hit (a raycast's hit.position / hit.normal, onCollide's contact.position / contact.normal); size meters ([start, end] ramps over the lifetime); rotation DEGREES (omit: random); lifetime seconds (Infinity: it never fades); fade the seconds at the end of the lifetime over which the mark fades (2 when omitted, at most the lifetime); attachTo: the object the mark rides; the mark ends when that object is destroyed position: Vec3 normal: Vec3 texture: string size?: number | [number, number] | [number | [number, number], number | [number, number]] = 0.5 rotation?: number | [number, number] lifetime?: number = 30 fade?: number color?: Color opacity?: number | [number, number] = 1 attachTo?: string } slash: { // a sweep-revealed arc at the ATTACKER's position; size METERS end-to-end, required (a sword ~2–3, a boss cleave 5+); default orientation horizontal at the caller's yaw, rotation in degrees; bands body / edge / fade 0..1; attachTo: <id> the slash rides that object: position, rotation and velocity are read in the world at the emit, then it moves and turns with the object and ends with it (a spin attack's ring that stays on the moving player) position: Vec3 size?: number shape?: "tightUniform" | "broadUniform" | "tightWidening" | "broadWidening" | "crescent" | "longCrescent" | "circle" noise?: "none" | "forward" | "backward" | "stableDissolve" glow?: "none" | "light" | "medium" | "intense" | "max" timing?: "quick" | "standard" | "slow" | "verySlow" body?: number edge?: number fade?: number edgeColor?: Color edgeAlpha?: number bodyColor1?: Color bodyColor1Alpha?: number bodyColor2?: Color bodyColor2Alpha?: number bodyColor3?: Color bodyColor3Alpha?: number outwardGlow?: number outwardGlowWidth?: number outwardGlowSpeed?: number rotation?: { yaw?: number; pitch?: number; roll?: number } velocity?: { x?: number; y?: number; z?: number } scaleVelocity?: number rotationVelocity?: { yaw?: number; pitch?: number; roll?: number } attachTo?: string } shockwave: { // an expanding ring of distortion that also lays the ground cover flat as it passes (the ring reaches scale / 2 m from position, from the ground up); speed (negative implodes), thickness / edgeFade 0..1, intensity 0 or more, scale in world units; easing "easeOut" for impacts position: Vec3 speed?: number = 0.5 thickness?: number = 0.5 intensity?: number = 0.5 edgeFade?: number = 0.5 scale?: number = 1 easing?: "linear" | "easeOut" | "easeIn" = "linear" } screenShake: { intensity: number; duration?: number = 0.2; haptic?: boolean = true } // the view shakes for each player who hears it, and that player's connected controller rumbles once with it (a phone in the Spawn app buzzes); `haptic: false` keeps the shake and drops the buzz screenFlash: { color?: Color; duration?: number = 0.15; intensity?: number = 0.35 } // a brief color wash; a rare beat (a death, a boss entry), never per hit: repeats strobe; intensity is the peak opacity, 0..1 hitstop: { duration: number; haptic?: boolean = true } // freeze the camera for `duration` seconds; the player's connected controller gives one short rumble with it (a phone in the Spawn app buzzes); `haptic: false` keeps the freeze and drops the buzz cameraPunch: { direction: Vec3; intensity?: number = 0.3 } // a directional camera kick: direction camera-local (x right, y up, z forward), intensity 0..1 (1 = a 12 cm kick); it rises over ~36 ms and settles by 180 ms slowMo: { scale: number; duration: number; easing?: boolean | string; grade?: boolean } // the picture slows to `scale` (0 holds it still, at most 1; a faster world is ctx.place.timeScale) for `duration` seconds under a desaturated grade, then catches up; the game keeps full speed; `grade: false` slows it in its own colours replay: { // this screen replays [from, to] (ms on ctx.now()'s clock; from at most 10 s back, at most 30 s long) as it drew it, through `camera` (a ViewCamera; omitted: its camera then), at `scale` x real speed (0 or more: 2 plays it twice as fast, 0 holds its first frame until the next replay; omitted: 1), then returns to live; while it plays, a REPLAY mark shows in the screen's corner and the game's HUD hides (`cue: false` drops the mark, `hud: true` keeps the HUD) from: number to: number camera?: ViewCameraPose | { parent: string; eye?: Vec3; aim?: Vec3 | "forward" | string; fov?: number; projection?: "perspective" | "orthographic"; orthoSize?: number; layers?: string[] } scale?: number cue?: boolean hud?: boolean } zoomTo: { // the camera moves to look at a point or an object, holds `hold` seconds, returns target: Vec3 | string duration?: number = 0.5 easing?: string = "easeOut" offset?: Vec3 hold?: number } flash: { target: string; color?: Color; duration?: number = 0.1; intensity?: number = 0.9 } // a brief emissive flash on an object: the per-hit feedback; intensity 0..1 (~0.45 on a mesh that fills the screen) shake: { target: string; intensity: number; duration: number } squash: { target: string; axis?: "x" | "y" | "z" = "y"; intensity?: number = 0.3; duration?: number = 0.15 } // intensity 0..1 (out of range clamps): at 1 the axis squashes to 5 % and the other two bulge by half; duration seconds impulse: { target: string; impulse?: Vec3; position?: Vec3; angularImpulse?: Vec3 } // a one-shot physics kick, applied exactly once to the target: `impulse` N·s at the center of mass, `position` moves where it lands (world point: off-center adds the spin), `angularImpulse` N·m·s of pure spin. At least one of impulse/angularImpulse. Dynamic bodies, ragdolls and characters take it; static and kinematic bodies take none. Reach for it when mass should matter or the hit lands off-center; a mass-independent push is `<entity>.velocity = v`. The held sibling is `ctx.self.forces` highlightSet: { // holds until highlightClear, or `duration` seconds; the line hides where its target hides; style "xray" = a faint thin line only where a wall or building hides the target; width = the line's width in pixels (of a 1080p picture) up close, omitted = the style's own: 2 for outline, about 16 for glow and pulse; intensity = the line's glow strength, 0 = none; omitted: 8 glow and pulse, 4 xray, outline its colour; the color's alpha is the line's opacity target: string color?: Color style?: "outline" | "glow" | "pulse" | "xray" = "outline" duration?: number width?: number intensity?: number } highlightClear: { target: string } outlinePage: { color?: Color; duration?: number = 0.45; width?: number = 3; pulses?: number = 1 } // pulse the page border: mode changes, confirmations; duration seconds, width pixels; a border wide enough to count as a flash pulses at most three times a second uiEvent: { name: string; payload?: unknown } // a once-only signal into ui.js (`window.spawn.on("event", (name, payload) => …)`): speech, a sound from ui code, anything "do this now, once"; never saved, never replayed; payload any JSON haptic: { // one buzz on the player's phone in the Spawn app, and on a connected controller whose motors the browser can drive; screenShake and hitstop buzz the phone and the controller on their own unless they say `haptic: false`, and footsteps, jumps and landings buzz the phone alone. A rumble of your own is the Gamepad API's playEffect, its effect type in `kind`, times in ms; both motors at 0 stops it kind: HapticKind | "dual-rumble" | "trigger-rumble" startDelay?: number duration?: number strongMagnitude?: number weakMagnitude?: number leftTrigger?: number rightTrigger?: number } milestone: { step?: number; name?: string } // how far a player got (a level, a checkpoint, a boss beaten): `step` its order 1, 2, 3 …, `name` your words (at most 40 characters), either is enough; counted once per player, and the game's numbers page draws how far new players get, step by step. A game keeps 100 milestone names: a new name past them is not counted, and getLogs says so stat: { name: string; value?: number; by?: string; vs?: string } // a number for this player (coins picked up, a fall; `value` omitted counts 1): the game's numbers page charts each name's daily total. A negative `value` is spent. `by` splits it by one of your words (where coins came from or went: `{ name: "coins", value: -120, by: "skins" }`), and each player's running total of a stat split by `by` is what they hold. `vs` beside `by` counts a win of `by` over `vs` (a fight's end: `{ name: "wins", by: winner, vs: loser }`), which the page draws as win rates and matchups. `name`, `by` and `vs` are at most 40 characters; a game keeps 100 stat names and 100 parts (each `by`, or `by` and `vs`) a stat: a new name past them is not counted, a new part counts with no split, and getLogs says so voxelMarkSet: { // an outline / fill overlay on one voxel cell (a build cursor, a target), never a terrain edit; omit both for the default outline markId: string voxel: VoxelCoord outline?: VoxelMarkOutlineOptions | null fill?: VoxelMarkFillOptions | null pulse?: VoxelMarkPulseOptions | null duration?: number } voxelMarkClear: { markId: string } partyAdd: { player: string | { readonly id: string } } // asks that player (a row, a hook's player, a ctx.place.players row, or its id) into your Spawn party, the plate's own ask: they join by their own yes, and you lead it (a party is made when you have none); friends both ways, so a guest (isGuest) neither asks nor is asked; one already in a party is refused. Your own word: emit it where ctx.self is your player partyCancel: { player: string | { readonly id: string } } // takes back the Spawn party ask your party sent that player (a row, a hook's player, a ctx.place.players row, or its id), the card's own take back: their ask leaves Spawn and a join after it is refused; one who already said yes stays in the party. The leader's word: emit it where ctx.self is your player partyLeave: {} // you leave your Spawn party, the card's own leave: a leader's leave hands the lead on, and the last one out ends it. Your own word: emit it where ctx.self is your player; it removes no one else partyJoin: { player: string | { readonly id: string } } // your yes to the Spawn party ask that player (a row, a hook's player, a ctx.place.players row, or its id) sent you, the ask's own join: you join their party, and a party of yours with others in it is left first. Spawn still shows its ask. Once per press of the player's: emit it from their onInput, where ctx.self is that player; with no press, or no ask from that player, it joins nothing partyPortal: {} // the party card's portal together: you, its leader, ask your party to where you stand, and each comes by their own press of Spawn's line. Once per press of the player's: emit it from their onInput, where ctx.self is that player guildAdd: { player: string | { readonly id: string } } // adds that player to your Spawn guild, the plate's own invite: any member's word; friends both ways guildKick: { player: string | { readonly id: string } } // removes that player from your guild: the leader removes anyone, an officer removes members guildRank: { player: string | { readonly id: string }; rank: "member" | "officer" } // sets that player's rank in your guild, the leader's word: member or officer (the lead is handed on the plate, never by a game) openSettings: { page?: "sound" | "voice" | "look" | "keys" | "screen" | "live" } // opens Spawn's settings plate, the gear's, once per press of the player's: emit it from their onInput, where ctx.self is that player; with no press it opens nothing. page "keys" opens it at the game's keys (a touch screen has none and opens the first page); another page opens it at that part, where this device draws it openAvatarEditor: {} // opens the player's own avatar editor, Spawn's, where they change the body they wear in every world: its own door over the game, never a settings page; once per press of the player's: emit it from their onInput, where ctx.self is that player; with no press it opens nothing. A guest is asked to sign in openInvite: {} // opens Spawn's invite over the game: the player's friends and their own link to here; once per press of the player's: emit it from their onInput, where ctx.self is that player. A guest is asked to sign in. The game never holds the link openShare: {} // opens Spawn's share of this game over the game: the game's link, in the phone's own share sheet or copied on a computer; once per press of the player's: emit it from their onInput, where ctx.self is that player. The game never holds the link }

ActPayloads = {
  damageNumber: {   // a number `value` or any string `text` ("MISS", "+4 tomatoes"): one is enough; red below 0; `lifetime` the seconds it stays
    position: Vec3
    value?: number
    text?: string
    color?: Color
    crit?: boolean
    size?: number = 1
    lifetime?: number = 1.5
  }
  playSound: {   // answers the sound's handle: emit("stopSound", { soundId }) ends it, loops included; with `position` it is heard from that spot at `volume` out to refDistance (default a sixth of maxDistance, at least 4 m and at most half of it), falling to silence at maxDistance (the audible reach in meters); without one it is the acting player's own; mode "restart" replaces this object's still-playing copy of that clip instead of stacking
    clip: string
    position?: Vec3
    volume?: number = 1
    pitch?: number = 1
    loop?: boolean
    mode?: "overlap" | "restart"
    bus?: string
    priority?: number
    maxDistance?: number
    refDistance?: number
    follow?: boolean
    onPlaying?: string | ((ctx: ObjectAPI, sound: { soundId: string; clip: string; durationSeconds?: number }) => unknown)   // an export of this script, run once as (ctx, sound) when the sound's first sample plays; durationSeconds is absent while the clip's length is unknown
  }
  stopSound: { soundId: string }
  preload: { refs: string[] }   // warms each sound, texture or model before its first use on the machines that hear it (the acting player's by default), so a game loads ahead of a moment it sees coming: emit it when those assets become likely; only machines in the room when it is sent hear it, so a room with no player in it warms no player, and one that joins later is not warmed; fire-and-forget, nothing shown, the world unchanged
  fx: {   // an effect script you wrote (scripts/effects/*.fx.js) spawned as an OBJECT at a point, answers its id (tagged "fx"): patch it through getObject(id).fx.params.heat = 0.2 (the effect re-runs), end a loop with destroy(id) (a finished one-shot removes itself); params / seed feed the effect export; attachTo: <id> parents it to that object: it appears at `position`, rides the target's transform and dies with it (the impact pattern: a burn on whatever the projectile hit)
    position: Vec3
    script: string
    params?: Record<string, unknown>
    seed?: number
    tags?: string[]
    attachTo?: string
  }
  decal: {   // a lasting mark projected onto the surface at the hit (a raycast's hit.position / hit.normal, onCollide's contact.position / contact.normal); size meters ([start, end] ramps over the lifetime); rotation DEGREES (omit: random); lifetime seconds (Infinity: it never fades); fade the seconds at the end of the lifetime over which the mark fades (2 when omitted, at most the lifetime); attachTo: the object the mark rides; the mark ends when that object is destroyed
    position: Vec3
    normal: Vec3
    texture: string
    size?: number | [number, number] | [number | [number, number], number | [number, number]] = 0.5
    rotation?: number | [number, number]
    lifetime?: number = 30
    fade?: number
    color?: Color
    opacity?: number | [number, number] = 1
    attachTo?: string
  }
  slash: {   // a sweep-revealed arc at the ATTACKER's position; size METERS end-to-end, required (a sword ~2–3, a boss cleave 5+); default orientation horizontal at the caller's yaw, rotation in degrees; bands body / edge / fade 0..1; attachTo: <id> the slash rides that object: position, rotation and velocity are read in the world at the emit, then it moves and turns with the object and ends with it (a spin attack's ring that stays on the moving player)
    position: Vec3
    size?: number
    shape?: "tightUniform" | "broadUniform" | "tightWidening" | "broadWidening" | "crescent" | "longCrescent" | "circle"
    noise?: "none" | "forward" | "backward" | "stableDissolve"
    glow?: "none" | "light" | "medium" | "intense" | "max"
    timing?: "quick" | "standard" | "slow" | "verySlow"
    body?: number
    edge?: number
    fade?: number
    edgeColor?: Color
    edgeAlpha?: number
    bodyColor1?: Color
    bodyColor1Alpha?: number
    bodyColor2?: Color
    bodyColor2Alpha?: number
    bodyColor3?: Color
    bodyColor3Alpha?: number
    outwardGlow?: number
    outwardGlowWidth?: number
    outwardGlowSpeed?: number
    rotation?: { yaw?: number; pitch?: number; roll?: number }
    velocity?: { x?: number; y?: number; z?: number }
    scaleVelocity?: number
    rotationVelocity?: { yaw?: number; pitch?: number; roll?: number }
    attachTo?: string
  }
  shockwave: {   // an expanding ring of distortion that also lays the ground cover flat as it passes (the ring reaches scale / 2 m from position, from the ground up); speed (negative implodes), thickness / edgeFade 0..1, intensity 0 or more, scale in world units; easing "easeOut" for impacts
    position: Vec3
    speed?: number = 0.5
    thickness?: number = 0.5
    intensity?: number = 0.5
    edgeFade?: number = 0.5
    scale?: number = 1
    easing?: "linear" | "easeOut" | "easeIn" = "linear"
  }
  screenShake: { intensity: number; duration?: number = 0.2; haptic?: boolean = true }   // the view shakes for each player who hears it, and that player's connected controller rumbles once with it (a phone in the Spawn app buzzes); `haptic: false` keeps the shake and drops the buzz
  screenFlash: { color?: Color; duration?: number = 0.15; intensity?: number = 0.35 }   // a brief color wash; a rare beat (a death, a boss entry), never per hit: repeats strobe; intensity is the peak opacity, 0..1
  hitstop: { duration: number; haptic?: boolean = true }   // freeze the camera for `duration` seconds; the player's connected controller gives one short rumble with it (a phone in the Spawn app buzzes); `haptic: false` keeps the freeze and drops the buzz
  cameraPunch: { direction: Vec3; intensity?: number = 0.3 }   // a directional camera kick: direction camera-local (x right, y up, z forward), intensity 0..1 (1 = a 12 cm kick); it rises over ~36 ms and settles by 180 ms
  slowMo: { scale: number; duration: number; easing?: boolean | string; grade?: boolean }   // the picture slows to `scale` (0 holds it still, at most 1; a faster world is ctx.place.timeScale) for `duration` seconds under a desaturated grade, then catches up; the game keeps full speed; `grade: false` slows it in its own colours
  replay: {   // this screen replays [from, to] (ms on ctx.now()'s clock; from at most 10 s back, at most 30 s long) as it drew it, through `camera` (a ViewCamera; omitted: its camera then), at `scale` x real speed (0 or more: 2 plays it twice as fast, 0 holds its first frame until the next replay; omitted: 1), then returns to live; while it plays, a REPLAY mark shows in the screen's corner and the game's HUD hides (`cue: false` drops the mark, `hud: true` keeps the HUD)
    from: number
    to: number
    camera?: ViewCameraPose | { parent: string; eye?: Vec3; aim?: Vec3 | "forward" | string; fov?: number; projection?: "perspective" | "orthographic"; orthoSize?: number; layers?: string[] }
    scale?: number
    cue?: boolean
    hud?: boolean
  }
  zoomTo: {   // the camera moves to look at a point or an object, holds `hold` seconds, returns
    target: Vec3 | string
    duration?: number = 0.5
    easing?: string = "easeOut"
    offset?: Vec3
    hold?: number
  }
  flash: { target: string; color?: Color; duration?: number = 0.1; intensity?: number = 0.9 }   // a brief emissive flash on an object: the per-hit feedback; intensity 0..1 (~0.45 on a mesh that fills the screen)
  shake: { target: string; intensity: number; duration: number }
  squash: { target: string; axis?: "x" | "y" | "z" = "y"; intensity?: number = 0.3; duration?: number = 0.15 }   // intensity 0..1 (out of range clamps): at 1 the axis squashes to 5 % and the other two bulge by half; duration seconds
  impulse: { target: string; impulse?: Vec3; position?: Vec3; angularImpulse?: Vec3 }   // a one-shot physics kick, applied exactly once to the target: `impulse` N·s at the center of mass, `position` moves where it lands (world point: off-center adds the spin), `angularImpulse` N·m·s of pure spin. At least one of impulse/angularImpulse. Dynamic bodies, ragdolls and characters take it; static and kinematic bodies take none. Reach for it when mass should matter or the hit lands off-center; a mass-independent push is `<entity>.velocity = v`. The held sibling is `ctx.self.forces`
  highlightSet: {   // holds until highlightClear, or `duration` seconds; the line hides where its target hides; style "xray" = a faint thin line only where a wall or building hides the target; width = the line's width in pixels (of a 1080p picture) up close, omitted = the style's own: 2 for outline, about 16 for glow and pulse; intensity = the line's glow strength, 0 = none; omitted: 8 glow and pulse, 4 xray, outline its colour; the color's alpha is the line's opacity
    target: string
    color?: Color
    style?: "outline" | "glow" | "pulse" | "xray" = "outline"
    duration?: number
    width?: number
    intensity?: number
  }
  highlightClear: { target: string }
  outlinePage: { color?: Color; duration?: number = 0.45; width?: number = 3; pulses?: number = 1 }   // pulse the page border: mode changes, confirmations; duration seconds, width pixels; a border wide enough to count as a flash pulses at most three times a second
  uiEvent: { name: string; payload?: unknown }   // a once-only signal into ui.js (`window.spawn.on("event", (name, payload) => …)`): speech, a sound from ui code, anything "do this now, once"; never saved, never replayed; payload any JSON
  haptic: {   // one buzz on the player's phone in the Spawn app, and on a connected controller whose motors the browser can drive; screenShake and hitstop buzz the phone and the controller on their own unless they say `haptic: false`, and footsteps, jumps and landings buzz the phone alone. A rumble of your own is the Gamepad API's playEffect, its effect type in `kind`, times in ms; both motors at 0 stops it
    kind: HapticKind | "dual-rumble" | "trigger-rumble"
    startDelay?: number
    duration?: number
    strongMagnitude?: number
    weakMagnitude?: number
    leftTrigger?: number
    rightTrigger?: number
  }
  milestone: { step?: number; name?: string }   // how far a player got (a level, a checkpoint, a boss beaten): `step` its order 1, 2, 3 …, `name` your words (at most 40 characters), either is enough; counted once per player, and the game's numbers page draws how far new players get, step by step. A game keeps 100 milestone names: a new name past them is not counted, and getLogs says so
  stat: { name: string; value?: number; by?: string; vs?: string }   // a number for this player (coins picked up, a fall; `value` omitted counts 1): the game's numbers page charts each name's daily total. A negative `value` is spent. `by` splits it by one of your words (where coins came from or went: `{ name: "coins", value: -120, by: "skins" }`), and each player's running total of a stat split by `by` is what they hold. `vs` beside `by` counts a win of `by` over `vs` (a fight's end: `{ name: "wins", by: winner, vs: loser }`), which the page draws as win rates and matchups. `name`, `by` and `vs` are at most 40 characters; a game keeps 100 stat names and 100 parts (each `by`, or `by` and `vs`) a stat: a new name past them is not counted, a new part counts with no split, and getLogs says so
  voxelMarkSet: {   // an outline / fill overlay on one voxel cell (a build cursor, a target), never a terrain edit; omit both for the default outline
    markId: string
    voxel: VoxelCoord
    outline?: VoxelMarkOutlineOptions | null
    fill?: VoxelMarkFillOptions | null
    pulse?: VoxelMarkPulseOptions | null
    duration?: number
  }
  voxelMarkClear: { markId: string }
  partyAdd: { player: string | { readonly id: string } }   // asks that player (a row, a hook's player, a ctx.place.players row, or its id) into your Spawn party, the plate's own ask: they join by their own yes, and you lead it (a party is made when you have none); friends both ways, so a guest (isGuest) neither asks nor is asked; one already in a party is refused. Your own word: emit it where ctx.self is your player
  partyCancel: { player: string | { readonly id: string } }   // takes back the Spawn party ask your party sent that player (a row, a hook's player, a ctx.place.players row, or its id), the card's own take back: their ask leaves Spawn and a join after it is refused; one who already said yes stays in the party. The leader's word: emit it where ctx.self is your player
  partyLeave: {}   // you leave your Spawn party, the card's own leave: a leader's leave hands the lead on, and the last one out ends it. Your own word: emit it where ctx.self is your player; it removes no one else
  partyJoin: { player: string | { readonly id: string } }   // your yes to the Spawn party ask that player (a row, a hook's player, a ctx.place.players row, or its id) sent you, the ask's own join: you join their party, and a party of yours with others in it is left first. Spawn still shows its ask. Once per press of the player's: emit it from their onInput, where ctx.self is that player; with no press, or no ask from that player, it joins nothing
  partyPortal: {}   // the party card's portal together: you, its leader, ask your party to where you stand, and each comes by their own press of Spawn's line. Once per press of the player's: emit it from their onInput, where ctx.self is that player
  guildAdd: { player: string | { readonly id: string } }   // adds that player to your Spawn guild, the plate's own invite: any member's word; friends both ways
  guildKick: { player: string | { readonly id: string } }   // removes that player from your guild: the leader removes anyone, an officer removes members
  guildRank: { player: string | { readonly id: string }; rank: "member" | "officer" }   // sets that player's rank in your guild, the leader's word: member or officer (the lead is handed on the plate, never by a game)
  openSettings: { page?: "sound" | "voice" | "look" | "keys" | "screen" | "live" }   // opens Spawn's settings plate, the gear's, once per press of the player's: emit it from their onInput, where ctx.self is that player; with no press it opens nothing. page "keys" opens it at the game's keys (a touch screen has none and opens the first page); another page opens it at that part, where this device draws it
  openAvatarEditor: {}   // opens the player's own avatar editor, Spawn's, where they change the body they wear in every world: its own door over the game, never a settings page; once per press of the player's: emit it from their onInput, where ctx.self is that player; with no press it opens nothing. A guest is asked to sign in
  openInvite: {}   // opens Spawn's invite over the game: the player's friends and their own link to here; once per press of the player's: emit it from their onInput, where ctx.self is that player. A guest is asked to sign in. The game never holds the link
  openShare: {}   // opens Spawn's share of this game over the game: the game's link, in the phone's own share sheet or copied on a computer; once per press of the player's: emit it from their onInput, where ctx.self is that player. The game never holds the link
}
